glossary: PE / put option
A bet that Nifty will fall. Buying one pays if it falls; selling one pays you upfront and costs you if it falls.
CE / call option
A bet that Nifty will rise.
Lot
Nifty options trade in lots of 65 units. ₹1 of option price = ₹65 per lot.
Put spread
Sell one put, buy a cheaper one below it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
15-min candle close
Wait for the 15-minute bar on the chart to finish before acting, so one spike doesn't fool you.
Call spread
Sell one call, buy a cheaper one above it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
Iron condor
A call spread and a put spread sold together. You collect both premiums; it pays if Nifty stays between the two sold strikes, and the loss is capped.

simple.headline: Bank Nifty drifted back to 61,985, right on the 62,000 line where buyers and sellers are evenly matched; wait for a clear move.
simple.do: Only if Bank Nifty rises to 62,250–62,350 and a full 15-minute candle fails to close above 62,350, place the spread; take profit when it slips back to 61,950.
simple.dont: Don't sell at 61,985; big traders added 4,000 bets in the last half hour that it won't fall below 62,000. Don't buy call options.
simple.stop: If a 15-minute candle closes above 62,450, close the trade and stay out of Bank Nifty for the day.

trade.name: Makes money if Bank Nifty stays below 62,300 till Monday 23 Nov
legs: SELL 1 lot  Bank Nifty 23-Nov  62,300 CE  at about ₹329
BUY  1 lot  Bank Nifty 23-Nov  62,500 CE  at about ₹258
trade.maxLoss: The most you can lose: ₹3,870 (129 points × 30)
trade.when: These are 10:45 prices; they will move. If you sold the 9:45 spread (62,200/62,400), keep it and use its 62,300 stop. Otherwise enter only after a rise to 62,250–62,350 stalls for 15 minutes.
trade.exit: Close both legs if a 15-minute candle closes above 62,450, or once you have kept half of the ₹2,130.

why: Since the open big traders placed 59,000 new bets that Bank Nifty won't rise, about twice the bets that it won't fall, so sellers still have the edge higher up.
But in the last half hour 4,000 new bets came in that it won't fall below 62,000, right at the current price, so selling here is fighting the floor.
The biggest bet of the day, 12,400 contracts, says it stays under 62,000 by Monday, and the price is sitting exactly there; that is a tug of war, so wait.
Option prices point to a move of about 400 points either way today, so a rise to 62,300 is possible; that is where you sell, not at 62,000.
simple.risk: Trade one lot only. ₹3,870 is the most you can lose, more than the ₹2,130 you collect, so honour the 62,450 stop. Bank Nifty moves 400 points in minutes. Paper-trade two weeks before real money.
glossary: PE / put option
A bet that Nifty will fall. Buying one pays if it falls; selling one pays you upfront and costs you if it falls.
CE / call option
A bet that Nifty will rise.
Lot
Bank Nifty options trade in lots of 30 units. ₹1 of option price = ₹30 per lot.
Put spread
Sell one put, buy a cheaper one below it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
15-min candle close
Wait for the 15-minute bar on the chart to finish before acting, so one spike doesn't fool you.
Call spread
Sell one call, buy a cheaper one above it. You collect money, and your loss is capped.
